source_text:
ἴδια αὐτῶν δεῖπνα ἐπείγοντο, ἅπερ πολυτελῶς ἐποίουν ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ὥσπερ
ἐλέγχοντες τῶν οὐκ ἐχόντων τὴν ἔνδειαν, διότι ἄλλων πεινώντων αὐτοὶ ἐμέθυον·
φθάνοντες γὰρ τὴν κοινωνίαν ἀπήλαυον τῶν ἰδίων ὄψων. 1 Kor 12,1–2 Πνευματικὰ
λέγει νῦν τὰς τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐνεργείας ἃς ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν ἀξίαν διερεῖ, οἷον
τῷ μὲν εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, τῷ δὲ προφητεύειν, καὶ ἑτέρῳ ἕτερον. διὰ δὲ τοῦ εἰπεῖν πρὸς
τὰ εἴδωλα ἀνήγεσθε δείκνυσι διαφορὰν προφητείας καὶ μαντείας μεγίστην. ἐν μὲν
γὰρ τοῖς εἰδώλοις οὐ νήφουσιν οἱ κάτοχοι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ πνεύματι, ἀλλ' ἀνάγονται
ὑπ' ἀκαθάρτου πνεύματος οὐκ αὐθαιρέτῳ γνώμῃ πορευόμενοι· τοῦτο γὰρ δηλοῖ διὰ
τοῦ ἀνήγεσθε ἀπαγόμενοι. φησὶ γοῦν· τὴν μὲν τοῦ ἀκαθάρτου πνεύματος ἐξ ὧν
ἐπάσχετε ἴστε ἐνέργειαν, τὰ δὲ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος καθαρὰν ἔχει τὴν ἐνέργειαν. διὸ
ὁ μὲν μάντις σκοτοῦται τὴν ψυχὴν καὶ οὐκ οἶδεν ὃ λέγει, τοῦ δὲ προφήτου ἡ ψυχὴ
φωτεινοτέρα γίνεται καὶ μαθοῦσα ἃ οὐκ ᾔδει λέγει τὰ ἀποκαλυφθέντα αὐτῇ. ὁ οὖν
δαίμων ὡς ἐχθρὸς σκοτεῖ τὴν ψυχήν, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ὡς εὐεργετικὸν φωτίζει
προσερχόμενον τῇ ψυχῇ, ὅπερ δεικνὺς ἐπάγει. 263 1 Kor 12,3 Πάντων γὰρ τὰ
βλάσφημα εἰς Χριστὸν ὑπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἐνεργεῖται τοῦ θολοῦντος τὴν ψυχήν. τοῦτο
οὖν λέγει ἀσφαλιζόμενος τοὺς προσποιουμένους θεοφορεῖσθαι καὶ κατὰ Χριστοῦ
λαλοῦντας. ἐπειδὴ δὲ καὶ ἡ λεγεὼν καὶ ἡ πυθομάντις ὠνόμαζον τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν,
οὐ λέγομεν ὅτι ὁ τοῦτο λέγων τελείως λέγει–εἰσὶ γὰρ πολλοὶ κύριοι λεγόμενοι
δίκαιοι–ἀλλὰ τὸ ὁμολογῆσαι τὴν ἐπὶ πάντων κυριότητα καὶ δεσποτείαν τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
ἴσως δὲ ὅτι καὶ πειρώμενοι τοῦτο ἔλεγον ὡς ὁ διάβολος ἀναγαγὼν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ ὄρος.
διὸ οὔτε ὥσπερ ἀναξίων καὶ πειραζόντων καταδέχεται τὴν ἐξ αὐτῶν μαρτυρίαν. 1
Kor 12,8–10 Λόγος σοφίας τὸ καὶ νοῆσαι τὰ ἐν σοφίᾳ θεοῦ εἰρημένα ἐν προφήταις καὶ
εὐαγγελισταῖς καὶ παραστῆσαι τοῖς ἀκούουσιν. λόγος γνώσεως ἡ ἀποκάλυψις τῶν
λανθανόντων ἃ μανθάνει τις μὴ εἰδὼς ἐν πρώτοις παρὰ τῆς τῆς χάριτος καὶ λέγει.
πίστις τὸ πιστεῦσαι μόνον τῷ κηρύγματι· οὐ γὰρ τὸ ἀκοῦσαι ἁπλῶς τοῦτο πίστις
ἀλλὰ τὸ δέξασθαι πιστῶς τὰ εἰρημένα. διάκρισις πνευμάτων, ἐπειδὴ μεμίμηται ἡ
μαντεία τὴν προφητείαν ἐν τῷ καὶ αὐτῇ δοκεῖν προλέγειν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, καὶ
τούτων τὴν διάκρισιν δέδωκεν διὰ τὸ μὴ πλανᾶσθαι. 1 Kor 12,12 Τῷ ὅλῳ σώματι ἐκ
πολλῶν συγκειμένῳ μελῶν ἀπεικονίζει τὸν Χριστόν, διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν
δηλῶν· ἐπεὶ γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς εἴρηται τῆς ἐκκλησίας κεφαλὴ καὶ ἡ ἐκκλησία σῶμα
Χριστοῦ, Χριστὸν δὲ ὠνόμασεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, ἀπὸ τοῦ κρείττονος τὸ ἔλαττον
δηλῶν. 1 Kor 12,14 Τοῦτο λέγει, ἵνα μὴ τοὺς ταπεινοτέρους ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ
περιορῶσιν· κἂν γὰρ τῇ φύσει ἐλάττω τις ᾖ, ἀλλὰ τῷ κοινῷ τῆς ἐκκλησίας
συμβάλλεται. 1 Kor 12,27 Οὐκ εἶπεν μέλη ἐκ μελῶν, ἀλλὰ μέλη πολλὰ ἐκ μέλους
ἑνός· μέλος γὰρ ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῦ ὅλου σώματος. Οὐκ εἶπεν ἐκ μελῶν, ἀλλ' ἐκ μέλους·
ἓν γάρ ἐστιν μέλος ἡ κεφαλή, ὅς ἐστι Χριστός, ἡ κεφαλὴ τῆς ἐκκλησίας. Ἐπειδὴ
μελῶν μέμνηται καὶ σώματος, ἄρχεται ἀπὸ τοῦ τιμιωτέρου τῶν ἄλλων μελῶν τῶν
μετὰ τὴν κεφαλήν, τῶν ἀποστόλων. προφήτας δὲ λέγει τοὺς ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, οὐ τοὺς
ἐν νόμῳ. τρίτον διδασκάλους. μὴ θαυμάσῃς εἰ πρὸ τῶν τὰς ἰάσεις καὶ τὰς δυνάμεις
ἐπιτελούντων τέθειται διδάσκαλος· τὰ γὰρ σημεῖα ἵνα πιστευθῇ ἡ γνῶσις, ἡ δὲ
γνῶσις διὰ τῶν διδασκόντων παρίσταται. ἀντιλήψεις. τοῦτο ἀλλαχοῦ λέγει· ὁ
προϊστάμενος ἐν σπουδῇ. κυβερνήσεις· αἱ διοικήσεις αἱ ἐκκλησιαστικαί. 264,ξολ2
Κεφαλὴ τῆς ἐκκλησίας Χριστός, μεθ' ὃ μέλος δεύτερα μέλη φησὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους.
Οὐ τοὺς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ λέγει, ἀλλὰ τοὺς τῆς ἐκκλησίας. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο δείκνυσιν ὅτι μέγα
ἐφρόνουν ἐπὶ τῷ χαρίσματι τῶν γλωσσῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἄλλοις χαρίσμασιν.
δείκνυσιν οὖν ὅτι τὸ μέγιστον ἡ ἀγάπη ἐστίν· ἐκεῖνα μὲν γὰρ χαρίσματά ἐστιν καὶ
pass_a_gloss: [11:20-21 note, continued] ...to their own suppers they hurried, which they made lavishly in the church, as if exposing the need of those not having, because while others were hungry they themselves were drunk; for getting ahead of the communion they enjoyed their own delicacies. [Label 1 Kor 12,1-2] He now calls spiritual things the workings of the Holy Spirit, which he distributes to each according to worth, for example to one to evangelize, to another to prophesy, and to another another thing. And by saying 'you were led off to the idols' he shows a very great difference of prophecy and soothsaying. For at the idols those possessed by the unclean spirit are not sober, but are led off by an unclean spirit, not going by self-chosen judgment; for he shows this by 'you were led off', being carried away. He says then: you know the working of the unclean spirit from the things you suffered, but the [gifts] of the Holy Spirit have pure working. Therefore the soothsayer is darkened in the soul and does not know what he says, but the soul of the prophet becomes brighter and having learned what it did not know speaks the things revealed to it. So the demon as an enemy darkens the soul, but the Spirit as beneficent enlightens [it], coming to the soul; showing which he adds [the next words]. [Label 1 Kor 12,3] For the blasphemous things of all against Christ are worked by the evil one who muddies the soul. So he says this securing [them against] those pretending to be God-borne and speaking against Christ. And since both the Legion and the Pythian soothsayer named the Lord Jesus, we do not say that the one saying this says it perfectly (for there are many called lords, righteous men), but [what counts is] to confess the lordship and mastery of Christ over all. And perhaps because they said this testing, as the devil having led him up to the mountain. Therefore he does not accept the testimony from them, as of unworthy and testing ones. [Label 1 Kor 12,8-10] Word of wisdom: both to understand the things said in wisdom of God in prophets and evangelists and to present [them] to the hearers. Word of knowledge: the revelation of hidden things, which someone not knowing at first learns from (the) grace and speaks. Faith: only to believe the preaching; for simply to hear is not this faith, but to receive faithfully the things said. Discernment of spirits: since soothsaying imitated prophecy in that in it too the Holy Spirit seems to foretell, he has also given the discernment of these, because of not being led astray. [Label 1 Kor 12,12] By the whole body composed of many members he pictures Christ, by Christ showing the church; for since Christ is called head of the church and the church body of Christ, and he named the church Christ, showing the lesser from the greater. [Label 1 Kor 12,14] He says this so that they do not overlook the humbler in the church; for even if someone is lesser in nature, still he contributes to the common [good] of the church. [Label 1 Kor 12,27] He did not say members from members but many members from one member; for the head of the whole body is a member. [Not printed again: He did not say from members but from a member; for the head is one member, who is Christ, the head of the church.] [Same label, words on 12:28] Since he mentions members and body, he begins from the more honorable of the other members, those after the head, the apostles. And he calls prophets those in the church, not those in the law. Third, teachers. Do not wonder if a teacher has been placed before those performing healings and powers; for the signs [are] so that the knowledge may be believed, and the knowledge is presented through those teaching. Helps: this he says elsewhere: 'the one leading, with diligence'. Governments: the church administrations. [264 col2, not printed again: Christ is head of the church, after which member he says the apostles are second members. He does not mean those in the law, but those of the church.] [264 col2 continued, on 12:31, no label in the edition] Because of this he shows that they thought big about the gift of tongues, but also in the other gifts. So he shows that the greatest is love; for those are gifts, given also... [continues]
pass_b_english: …suppers of their own they hurried. These they laid on lavishly in the church, as if to show up the want of those who had nothing, since they got drunk while others went hungry. They got in ahead of the communion and enjoyed their own fine food.

On 1 Corinthians 12:1–2: By “spiritual gifts” he now means the workings of the Holy Spirit, which he distributes to each according to worth: to one to preach the gospel, to another to prophesy, to another something else. By saying “you were led away to the idols,” he shows how very different prophecy is from soothsaying. At the idols, those possessed by the unclean spirit are not sober. They are carried off by the unclean spirit and do not go by their own free choice; that is what he shows by “you were led away,” carried off as they were. So he says: you know from what you went through how the unclean spirit works, but the gifts of the Holy Spirit work purely. So the soothsayer is darkened in soul and does not know what he is saying, while the prophet's soul grows brighter; it learns what it did not know and speaks what has been revealed to it. The demon, as an enemy, darkens the soul; the Spirit, as a benefactor, comes to the soul and gives it light. He goes on to show this.

On 1 Corinthians 12:3: Everything blasphemous against Christ is worked by the evil one, who clouds the soul. He says this to guard them against those who pretend to be carried by God and yet speak against Christ. Legion and the Pythian soothsayer both named the Lord Jesus, so we do not say that whoever says this says it perfectly, since many righteous men are called “lords.” What counts is to confess Christ's lordship and mastery over all. Perhaps, too, they said it to test him, as the devil did when he took him up onto the mountain (Matthew 4:8). That is why he does not accept their witness either, since it came from the unworthy and from those testing him.

On 1 Corinthians 12:8–10: “The word of wisdom” is to understand what was spoken in God's wisdom in the prophets and evangelists, and to set it before the hearers. “The word of knowledge” is the revelation of hidden things, which someone who did not know them at first learns from grace and then speaks. “Faith” is simply believing the preaching: merely hearing it is not faith; faith is receiving faithfully what has been said. “Discernment of spirits”: soothsaying has copied prophecy, in that in soothsaying too the Holy Spirit seems to foretell, so he has given the power to tell these apart, so that we are not led astray.

On 1 Corinthians 12:12: He pictures Christ by the whole body made up of many members, meaning the church by “Christ.” Christ is called the head of the church and the church the body of Christ, and here he has named the church “Christ,” pointing to the lesser by the greater.
On 1 Corinthians 12:14: He says this so that they do not look down on the humbler members of the church. Even if someone is lesser by nature, he still contributes to the common good of the church.
On 1 Corinthians 12:27: He did not say “members from members” but “many members from one member,” for the head of the whole body is a member.

On 1 Corinthians 12:28: Since he has spoken of members and a body, he starts from the most honored of the other members after the head, the apostles. By “prophets” he means those in the church, not those under the law. Third, teachers. Do not be surprised that the teacher is placed ahead of those who work healings and mighty deeds. The signs are there so that the knowledge may be believed, and the knowledge is set before people by those who teach. “Helps”: he speaks of this elsewhere: “he who leads, with diligence” (Romans 12:8). “Administrations”: the governing of the church.

On 1 Corinthians 12:31: For this reason he shows that they took great pride in the gift of tongues, and in the other gifts too. So he shows that love is the greatest thing. Those other gifts are given even…

choices.why: θολόω is to muddy or make turbid.
rejected: who thunders at the soul (old English)

choices.term: φθάνοντες γὰρ τὴν κοινωνίαν ἀπήλαυον τῶν ἰδίων ὄψων
choices.english: They got in ahead of the communion and enjoyed their own fine food
choices.why: φθάνω + acc. is to get ahead of; ὄψα are delicacies.
rejected: envying the fellowship, they deprived others of their own sight (old English)

choices.term: εἰσὶ γὰρ πολλοὶ κύριοι λεγόμενοι δίκαιοι
choices.why: Reading δίκαιοι as the subject class; 'lord' is a common courtesy title.
Apostles, prophets, teachers, helps, administrations are the words of 12:28.
The note quotes the 12:31 lemma (ποθεῖτε τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ κρείττονα); label taken from those words and noted.

bible_refs.note: labels checked against the words; 12:28 relabeled
